drug_class: MAO-B inhibitor (monoamine oxidase type B inhibitor)
purpose: Safinamide is used to treat Parkinson's disease. It is added to levodopa/carbidopa therapy when patients start experiencing 'off' episodes — times when their Parkinson's symptoms come back or get worse between doses. It helps give patients more 'on' time when their symptoms are better controlled.
how_it_works: Safinamide works by blocking an enzyme in the brain called MAO-B, which normally breaks down dopamine. By blocking this enzyme, more dopamine stays available in the brain for longer. Dopamine is the chemical messenger that helps control movement, and people with Parkinson's disease don't have enough of it.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include uncontrolled or involuntary movements (dyskinesia), nausea, falls, trouble sleeping, and feeling sleepy or drowsy. Some people may also notice dizziness or a runny nose.
warnings: Do not take safinamide with certain antidepressants (like SSRIs, SNRIs, tricyclics, or MAOIs) because a dangerous reaction called serotonin syndrome can occur. Avoid foods very high in tyramine (like aged cheeses, cured meats, or fermented foods) as this can cause a dangerous spike in blood pressure. Tell your doctor if you have liver problems, a history of impulse control issues, or vision problems, as safinamide can sometimes worsen these. Do not stop taking this medication suddenly without talking to your doctor first.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose is 50 mg taken by mouth once a day. After two weeks, your doctor may increase it to 100 mg once daily if needed and tolerated. It is taken at the same time each day, with or without food.
